Convert MeteoGalicia daily observations to functional data

Source: R/meteogal2fdata.R
meteogal2fdata.Rd

Construct an fda.usc::fdata object from one numeric meteorological variable, with one curve per station-year.

Usage

meteogal2fdata(
  station_id = NULL,
  var,
  start_date = NULL,
  end_date = NULL,
  last_n_days = 30L,
  df = NULL,
  file = NULL,
  output_file = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  control = list(),
  quality = c(1L, 5L)
)

Arguments

station_id

Optional station code(s); used to filter local data or to select stations for online requests.

var

A single numeric variable, e.g. "temp_mean" or "prec".

start_date, end_date

Optional initial and final date (YYYY-MM-DD or Date). For online requests, omitted dates default to the last 30 days.

last_n_days

Positive integer, for the default online interval.

df

Optional data.frame of daily observations.

file

Optional input file(s) or directory (outputs of meteogal2download(), or files saved with meteogal2df(file = ...)).

output_file

Optional .rds, .rda or .RData output path.

verbose

Print download or reading messages.

control

List of options passed to meteogal2df() for online data.

quality

Validation codes whose values are used (default c(1, 5)); see meteogal2df() and meteogal_qc_codes(). Values without a code (data without codes) are kept.

Value

An fdata object with one row per station-year (row names station_year), 365 columns, and attributes quality_summary, qc, fecha, quality_codes, var_name, var_units and source.

Details

Each curve has 365 common evaluation points (argvals = 1:365). February 29 is removed, and subsequent dates in leap years are shifted so that position 60 always represents March 1. Days without a record, and values not admitted by quality, are NA; nothing is imputed. Different stations and years are never combined in the same curve.

Supply either df (for example, from meteogal2df()), file (a .rda, .rds, .csv, or a directory), or neither to query MeteoGalicia online. output_file saves the result.

Per-curve information is attached as attributes whose row names are the curve names (station_year): quality_summary (counts per curve: original, interpolated, suspect, unvalidated, erroneous, not registered, unknown, valid, interp, masked, missing), qc (365-column matrix of validation codes) and fecha (365-column matrix with the date of every record). fda.usc subsetting (fd[i]) does not subset attributes, so after subsetting use attr(fd, "qc")[rownames(fd$data), ]. For analyses that need this metadata, meteogal2lfdata() is preferable: it keeps it in ldata$df, which is subset together with the curves.

Source: MeteoGalicia, Xunta de Galicia.

References

MeteoGalicia daily JSON service documentation: https://www.meteogalicia.gal/datosred/infoweb/meteo/docs/rss/JSON_EstacionsDiarios_es.pdf.

See also

meteogal2lfdata(), meteogal2df(), meteogal_qc_codes()

Examples

d <- data.frame(fecha = as.Date(c("2024-02-28", "2024-02-29", "2024-03-01")),
                station_id = "10157", temp_mean = c(11, 12, 13),
                qc_temp_mean = c(1L, 1L, 2L))
fd <- meteogal2fdata(var = "temp_mean", df = d)
#> [MeteoGalicia] quality = c(1, 5): values set to NA: 1 with code 2 (Suspect). Codes are kept in the qc_ columns; see meteogal_qc_codes().
dim(fd$data)
#> [1]   1 365
fd$data[1, 59:60]       # 11 (Feb 28), NA (Mar 1 is suspect, code 2)
#> 59 60 
#> 11 NA 
attr(fd, "qc")[1, 59:60]
#> 59 60 
#>  1  2 
attr(fd, "quality_summary")
#>            n_original n_interpolated n_suspect n_unvalidated n_erroneous
#> 10157_2024          1              0         1             0           0
#>            n_not_registered n_unknown n_valid n_interp n_masked n_missing
#> 10157_2024                0         0       1        0        1       364
